reviews.review:
The Jester and the Madman is a Point and Click adventure game that feels like it was plucked straight out of the 1990s. For better and for worse. There are no quality of life improvements or anything of the nature that feels modern. For those looking for a complete retro experience, you will probably enjoy this game. The story involves Lovecraftian Eldrich cult horror, but most of the game you are just exploring and solving puzzles in locations such as a hospital, a mansion, a farm, a few side streets and an underground cavern. There are 2 endings to the game, a bad ending if you play the game normally, and a secret good ending for solving a few extra puzzles. (Save often in different files) The game took approximately 2.5 hours to complete.

+ The voice acting in this game is excellent.
+ The sound effects and music in the game are retro and really fun to listen to.
+ There is a point system in the game that is great for replayability if you're a die hard adventure fan.
+ Several puzzles are very clever. The puzzles are very diverse in design.
+ The game is priced well at $5.00.
+ Some unexpected twists and turns in the story.
+ Well made retro stylized cutscenes.

- The game is very slow and retro, modern gamers might be bored at times.
- A few of the puzzles in the game are extremely obtuse and difficult to solve. Pure 1990's tradition. (There is a helpful guide in the Steam Guide section if you're stuck)

An excellent ode to 1990's adventure gaming, but be prepared for the same flaws that most of those games had back in the day.

Overall: 7.5/10
